import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_2.csv",

    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_4.csv",

    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_7.csv",

    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_9.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_10.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_11.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_12.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_13.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/training_14.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)  # ignore the first numerical index column
    # Ensure the 'title' column is integer type as per target schema
    df['title'] = df['title'].astype(int)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema ['title'] as the target,
# and the target schema is also ['title'], we can simply concatenate (union) all source tables.
# This satisfies Hint 2 and Hint 24.

# Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically (union)
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# The target examples show 25710 tuples, so no aggregation or grouping is needed.
# Just output the concatenated DataFrame as the target.

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_51/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
